_comment: Guided tour of the plugin manager. Every step points at a real control and waits for the user to press it -- watching a button being pressed does not teach anyone where it is.

steps.title: Everything ChiSurf found
steps.text: This table is one row per plugin. It is sorted and searchable: click a column header to sort, type in the search box to narrow it down, and right-click the header to show columns that start hidden — Id, Source and Window state among them.

steps.title: Pick one
steps.text: Select any row. The right-hand panel fills in with what that plugin is, which folder it lives in, and how it is wired to the rest.

await.hint: Click any row in the table.

steps.title: What it needs, and what needs it
steps.text:
The Requires column is what must load before this plugin — a module-level import. Required by is the reverse, and it is the one that matters before you switch anything off: those plugins stop working.

The Dependencies table lower down shows both directions at once, with the version bound and whether the plugin at the other end is actually installed.

steps.title: Switching a plugin off
steps.text: Disabled takes a plugin out of the menus without deleting anything. If other plugins require it, you are told which ones before the change sticks — that is what the reverse dependency index is for.

steps.title: Putting one to hand
steps.text: Show in main toolbar pins the selected plugin to the main window's toolbar, so you do not have to walk the menus to reach the tool you use every day.

steps.title: Installing something new
steps.text: 📥 Install… takes a plugin folder or a .zip. The manifest is validated first, so a broken plugin is refused with a reason instead of being copied in and silently ignored. It lands in your personal plugin directory (~/.chisurf/plugins), which needs no administrator rights.

steps.title: Nothing is saved until you say so
steps.text:
Changes here live in a working copy. Press 💾 Save to write them, or ♻️ Revert to throw them away. Menu changes appear the next time ChiSurf starts.

Try it now.

steps.title: Where to read more
steps.text: The ? button explains every control on this panel, and how plugin dependencies are declared in a manifest.
